entries.metric: Global club agent/intermediary service fees (men's professional football)
entries.caveat: Highest-ever annual total; +90% vs 2024's USD 710.4m; 2020 was USD 497.5m; 2016 was USD 386.8m.

Only 13-14 transfers involved. This figure appears to track fees paid by CAF-side ENGAGING (buying) clubs, not commission taken from departing African players - the wrong side of the transaction for an export-leakage metric, and far too small a sample to index on regardless. Reported here for transparency, not used in any computed metric.

entries.metric: Solidarity contributions actually paid vs. owed (compliance rate)
entries.source: Asser International Sports Law Blog (2020) citing FIFA Global Transfer Market Report 2019
entries.caveat: USD 67.7m paid of USD 351.5m owed globally. Six years old and global, not per-country or current - the only concrete solidarity-mechanism compliance figure found during research. Not used in any computed metric.

entries.source: Asser International Sports Law Blog (2020) citing FIFA Players' Status Department Report
entries.caveat: vs. 304 for CONMEBOL, despite CAF-to-UEFA transfer volume (581) being a meaningful share of within-UEFA volume (8108). Author's interpretation: African federations/clubs either lack awareness of these rights or cannot afford to pursue remedies. Illustrative context only.

not_an_index: None of these figures feed the FEFI composite. The originally-approved methodology planned to score 'value captured vs. leaked' quantitatively (agent commissions, solidarity/training compensation), but no current, country-level data exists to do that honestly - see /methodology.md 'Source verification findings'. These entries are the real numbers found, kept as cited, dated context instead of being forced into a score.
